note: Guide, not gospel. Item wording is a draft for pastoral review. 'orig' maps to the codes in the original GGBC questionnaire; 'status' says how much the wording changed.

formMetadata.title: Spiritual Gifts Discovery
formMetadata.introText: Answer honestly. Most people find some statements fit them and some do not. That is how we find what stands out for you.

completionMessage.heading: Thank you!
completionMessage.body: Pray about your results and talk with a leader you trust.

checkpointAfterStage1.message: Here are the gifts that stand out most for you so far.

actions.label: Stop here and save my results
Stop here and save my results

breatherMessages: Good work. You are doing well.
Keep going, you are making progress.

dataQuality.gentlePrompt: You are moving fast. Take a moment if any statement needs a closer look.

perCategory.note: Categories have different item counts, so use the mean, not the sum.

ranking.why: Some people agree with everything. Ranking by what stands out for the person keeps the top 3 meaningful.

highAgreementNotice.text: You agreed with most statements, so your list shows what stands out most for you compared with your other answers.

qualityProfile.note: Do not rank qualities against gifts. Use encouraging wording.

nextSteps: Talk with a trusted leader or mentor
Join a small group on my top gifts

Connect with someone who serves in my gift area
results.disclaimer: This is a starting point, not a final word. Gifts are confirmed over time by serving, by fruit, and by your church family (1 Cor 12:7).

groups.title: Gifts of the Spirit
groups.subtitle: The gifts listed in 1 Corinthians 12 and Romans 12
groups.intro: These statements are about gifts the Bible names in 1 Corinthians 12 and Romans 12. There are no right or wrong answers. Answer from your real life, not from how you wish you were.

categories.name: Wisdom
categories.description: Knowing what to do in a hard situation, and how God’s Word applies to it.

items.text: When a group is stuck on a decision, my idea is often the one people choose.
People come to me when they have a hard decision to make.
In a hard situation, I often know what should be done.
People have come back to tell me my advice was right for them.
I can see how a Bible truth applies to real-life problems.
I often see where a choice will lead before other people do.
I have helped someone through a big life decision using God’s Word.
I can see a way forward when other people feel lost.

categories.name: Knowledge
categories.description: Knowing things about people or situations that God shows you, which you could not have learned on your own.

items.text: I have known a fact about a person or situation that nobody told me, and it turned out to be true.
When I pray, I sometimes suddenly know something I did not know before.
I believe God has shown me specific things by His Spirit.
I notice spiritual things that other people miss.
What I learned in prayer has brought someone clarity or healing.
I have sensed the truth about a situation, and it was proven right later.

categories.name: Faith
categories.description: A deep, steady trust that God will act, which lifts the faith of others.

items.text: I stay sure that God can act, even when things look impossible.
I help other people trust God in hard times.
I have taken a step for God where I had to depend on Him completely.
I see ways to serve God where other people only see problems.
When a whole group feels discouraged about a project, I am usually still sure it can be done.
When I speak about God’s promises, other people’s faith grows.
I have prayed for something I believed God would do, and He did it.
I have committed to something for God that most people around me thought was risky or unwise.

categories.name: Healings
categories.description: Praying for the sick and seeing people get better.

items.text: I feel a strong need to pray for people who are sick or hurting.
I often feel pushed to pray for a certain person to be healed.
People have told me they got better after I prayed with them.
In the last 6 months, I have prayed in person with someone for healing, outside of a church service.
I feel very sure and bold when I pray for healing.
I keep praying for the sick even when I do not see results yet.
I check on people I have prayed for to see how they are doing.

categories.name: Miracles
categories.description: God doing powerful, unusual things through your prayers.

items.text: I have been there when something happened that experts said could not happen, after prayer.
I have seen answers to prayer that nobody could explain.
I pray boldly when a situation needs God to do something impossible.
I am very aware of God’s power at work around me.
I have seen God step in, in a surprising and powerful way.
Other people have said they clearly saw God’s power at work through my prayers.
I am comfortable praying for big breakthroughs.
I expect to see God do powerful things through my prayers and service.

categories.name: Prophecy
categories.description: Sharing a message from God that builds up, encourages, or comforts people.

items.text: I sometimes get a strong feeling that I should share a message from God.
During worship, I pick up what I think God’s Spirit is saying.
I have shared a message I believed was from God, and the person said it spoke to their exact situation.
My messages usually encourage, strengthen, or comfort people.
I have received a message from the Lord that later turned out to be true or helpful.

categories.name: Discerning of Spirits
categories.description: Sensing what is from God and what is not, and spotting what is false.

items.text: I can often sense when something is spiritually healthy or unhealthy.
I can tell the difference between God’s Spirit, human feelings, and other spiritual influences.
I notice problems in teaching or ministry before other people do.
I have sensed something was wrong with a person or situation before there was any proof, and I was later proven right.
I have raised a concern about a teaching or a person that others missed, and the concern was right.
I can sense the spiritual feeling in a room and what God is doing there.
I pray for wisdom to see lies and to help others find the truth.

categories.name: Tongues
categories.description: Praying in a spiritual language you have not learned.

items.text: I have spoken in tongues.
I pray in tongues several times a week.
In prayer or worship, I feel a pull to pray in tongues.
Praying in tongues makes me stronger in spirit and closer to God.
I sometimes pray in tongues for other people or situations.

categories.name: Interpretation of Tongues
categories.description: Understanding and explaining what is spoken in tongues, so that everyone is built up.

items.text: When someone speaks in tongues in a meeting, I sometimes get a sense of what it means.
I have received words or pictures in my mind that seemed to explain a message in tongues.
I have spoken out an interpretation in a gathering.
People have told me my interpretation helped or encouraged them.
When tongues are spoken in a meeting, I listen closely for the meaning.

categories.name: Service / Helps
categories.description: Doing practical work that makes it possible for others to do ministry.

items.text: I enjoy practical work that helps others do ministry well.
I would rather spend Sunday on setup and behind-the-scenes work than sit in the main service.
I quickly notice practical needs that other people miss.
When I see a job nobody has been given, I do it without being asked.
I feel happy when I help people get God’s work done.
People come to me when something needs to get done.
I enjoy behind-the-scenes work that supports leaders and events.
Routine practical jobs, like cleaning or carrying things, bore me.

categories.name: Teaching
categories.description: Explaining God’s Word clearly so people understand and grow.

items.text: I lose track of time when I prepare a Bible lesson.
I can explain Bible truths so that others understand.
People often ask me to explain hard Bible passages.
I enjoy preparing lessons, Bible studies, or teaching materials.
I can tell the difference between true Bible teaching and wrong teaching.
It really bothers me when people misunderstand an important Bible teaching.
I check carefully that what I teach is correct and based on Scripture.
I would rather explain a passage to a group than counsel one person about a personal problem.

categories.name: Encouragement
categories.description: Encouraging, motivating, and urging people forward in their faith.

items.text: People seek me out when they need encouragement to keep going.
I can correct someone gently and still leave them encouraged.
I often give people a clear next step, not just sympathy.
I move people to act on what the Bible says.
I can lift up someone who is discouraged, confused, or weak in faith.
I see the best in people and help them see it too.
I am drawn to people who need someone to believe in them.

categories.name: Giving
categories.description: Giving money and resources freely and cheerfully for God’s work.

items.text: I give well beyond what is expected, and I do not feel worried about it.
I often notice money or material needs that other people do not see.
I feel great joy when my money or things help God’s work.
Compared to what I earn, I have given a lot to meet a need that nobody asked me to meet.
I pray about how to use my money to do the most good for God’s kingdom.
I feel blessed when I can meet someone’s need by giving.
It is hard for me to give money away.

categories.name: Leadership
categories.description: Guiding people toward a goal and helping others grow as leaders.

items.text: People naturally look to me for direction.
I enjoy getting people to work together toward one goal.
I can see where a ministry should go and help others get there.
I am comfortable making an unpopular decision for the good of the group.
When a group is not sure what to do, I am the one who suggests a direction.
I enjoy training other leaders instead of keeping all the work to myself.
When someone needs to lead, I step up naturally.
I can inspire others to follow a vision.

categories.name: Administration
categories.description: Planning, organizing, and making things run well.

items.text: I naturally build plans or systems that make ministry work better.
I notice when important details have been missed.
I enjoy planning events, schedules, and activities.
I can handle many tasks at once without losing track.
Disorganization in a ministry bothers me enough that I fix it without being asked.
I like to see things done properly and with attention to detail.
I can see how to make a process faster or simpler.
I do not mind when plans are loose and some details get missed.

categories.name: Mercy
categories.description: Caring for people who are hurting, with kindness you can see.

items.text: I feel the pain of other people deeply, even people I barely know.
I am drawn to people who are hurting, rejected, or forgotten.
I enjoy visiting and caring for people going through hard times.
I stay kind to someone even after they have failed again and again.
I am happy to spend a lot of time listening to hurting people.
I often notice emotional needs that other people miss.
In the last month, I helped a hurting person even though it cost me time or comfort.
It is hard for me to listen to people’s problems for a long time.

categories.name: Apostolic / Pioneering
categories.description: Starting new works and opening new ground for the gospel.

items.text: I feel a strong burden to start new works for God’s kingdom.
I get energy from starting ministry where there are few Christians.
I can see what could be built where nothing exists yet.
I have started something new, such as a group, a ministry, or a church.
I feel restless when everything is already set up. I want to start something new.
I am comfortable going to unfamiliar places for the sake of the gospel.
I care deeply about God’s work growing beyond my own church.
I often dream about what God could do in new places.

groups.title: Gifts for Service & Ministry
groups.subtitle: Ways God equips people to serve and reach others
groups.intro: Now let's look at gifts that show up in how you serve and reach people. Again, answer from your real life.

categories.name: Evangelism
categories.description: Sharing the good news so that people come to know Jesus.

items.text: I enjoy talking with non-believers about Jesus.
I look for chances to share the gospel.
I can explain the gospel clearly to someone who is not a Christian.
In the last month, I started a conversation about Jesus with someone outside the church.
I am comfortable starting spiritual talks with strangers.
I have led someone to Christ or helped them take a step closer to Jesus.
Compared to most people I know, I bring up Jesus more in everyday conversation.
I avoid talking about Jesus with people outside the church.

categories.name: Pastoring / Shepherding
categories.description: Caring for people’s spiritual growth over the long term.

items.text: I think about certain people’s spiritual condition during the week without anyone reminding me.
I follow up on people who are missing, struggling, or weak in faith.
People trust me with their personal and spiritual problems.
I enjoy helping new believers get started and then grow over a long time.
I am patient as I walk with people through their growth.
I feel responsible for helping people become strong in Christ.
I keep real friendships with the people I care for spiritually.
I would rather spend an evening walking with one struggling person than speak to a large crowd.

categories.name: Missionary / Cross-Cultural
categories.description: Taking the gospel to other cultures and people groups.

items.text: I care deeply about people and communities outside my normal world.
I would change the way I live to serve people from another culture.
I want to take the gospel to places where Jesus is less known.
Cultural differences make me curious, not afraid.
I have taken real steps toward serving in another culture or region, like learning a language or asking questions about it.
I enjoy making friends across tribe, culture, or social background.
I have taken part in missions or cross-cultural ministry.
I feel called to serve God among a different people group.

categories.name: Hospitality
categories.description: Welcoming people and making them feel at home.

items.text: I enjoy welcoming people into my home or church.
Visitors often feel at ease around me.
I notice when someone is left out or feels unwelcome.
I enjoy preparing food or creating a place where people can relax and share life together.
I especially enjoy welcoming newcomers, strangers, and guests.
I invite people to my table or home more than most people I know.
I feel full of energy, not tired, after hosting people.
I make people feel at home and cared for.

categories.name: Intercession
categories.description: Praying for others for long periods, with a strong burden.

items.text: I often feel pushed to pray for a person or situation for a long time.
I keep praying even when I see no answer yet.
I often become aware of people or situations that need prayer.
I regularly pray for an hour or more without it feeling forced.
I have seen big answers to prayer after praying for a long time.
Prayer is one of my strongest ways of serving God.
I feel a burden to pray about big decisions that affect the church.
It is hard for me to keep praying for a long time.

categories.name: Worship / Music
categories.description: Leading others into God’s presence through music and worship.

items.text: I naturally show my love for God through music or singing.
I can help lead others into real worship.
I feel very aware of God’s presence during worship.
People have asked me to lead or play music for worship.
I practise music or worship skills on my own time, without being asked.
I can help create a place where people focus on God.
Music is a big part of how I live out and show my faith.
I am moved to worship, and I want to bring others in with me.

categories.name: Craftsmanship / Creative
categories.description: Using practical and creative skills to build, make, and serve.

items.text: I have practical or creative skills I can use for God’s work.
I enjoy building, designing, decorating, making, or fixing things for ministry.
I can turn an idea into something real and useful.
I feel satisfied when I use my skills to serve others.
I have given my skills (building, design, media, tech, sewing, and so on) to church projects without pay.
I have made something for the church that was useful or beautiful.
I love bringing ideas to life through my creativity.

categories.name: Deliverance / Spiritual Warfare
categories.description: Praying with people under spiritual attack so they can find freedom in Christ.

items.text: I feel a strong burden to pray for people who are under spiritual attack.
I notice when a situation may involve spiritual bondage.
I have stayed calm and prayed with someone in a frightening spiritual moment when others were afraid.
I am willing to pray with people who are struggling spiritually.
I have prayed for someone to be set free from spiritual bondage.

groups.title: Good Christian Qualities
groups.subtitle: Character that every believer is called to grow in
groups.intro: These are not gifts. They are qualities every believer should grow in. This part shows your strengths and where you can grow.

categories.name: Faithfulness
categories.description: Being someone others can depend on, in small things and big things.

items.text: I can be trusted to finish what I am given to do.
I stay committed even when ministry gets hard.
I am willing to serve in small tasks before I get bigger ones.
I do not need praise to stay committed to ministry.
Leaders can depend on me.
I believe being faithful matters as much as being gifted.
I keep the promises I make to the church.
The church can count on me to show up and do what needs to be done.

categories.name: Humility & Teachability
categories.description: Staying humble and open to correction, especially in spiritual things.

items.text: I am happy to have what I sense from God tested by Scripture and by my leaders.
I share what I sense with humility, and I never act more sure than I am.
I am careful not to mistake dislike or suspicion for spiritual discernment.
I stay quiet if I am not sure something is from God.
I am comfortable letting mature leaders weigh what I believe I have received.
I serve with humility and under the leadership of the church.
I give because I love God, not because I feel I have to.
I am open to the Holy Spirit leading me in how I use spiritual gifts.

categories.name: Rooted in Scripture
categories.description: Testing everything by the Bible and keeping spiritual things in good order.

items.text: I check spiritual impressions against the Bible.
I can tell the difference between my own thoughts and a prompting from God’s Spirit.
I understand that a prophecy must never go against Scripture.
I know that tongues in a church meeting must be used in an orderly way.
I know that an interpretation must agree with Scripture and build up the church.
I know that deliverance ministry needs Scripture, prayer, wisdom, and church oversight.
I want to see people set free in Christ, not to put on a show.
I believe God still heals today, as He did in the Bible.
